bibliographic.title: Balancing innovation and risk: artificial intelligence in travel medicine
bibliographic.venue: Tropical Diseases, Travel Medicine and Vaccines
bibliographic.citation_apa: van Genderen, P. J. J. (2026). Balancing innovation and risk: artificial intelligence in travel medicine. Tropical Diseases, Travel Medicine and Vaccines, 12, 24. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40794-026-00309-z

methodology.technology_context: Machine learning, generative AI, LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT), chatbots, and digital surveillance tools applied across the travel health continuum including pre-travel counselling, surveillance, and post-travel diagnosis

eligibility.decision_rationale: Perspective article in travel medicine that explicitly discusses LLMs and chatbots as travel health information tools, emphasizes clinical oversight, validation, explainability, accountability, governance, privacy, and regulatory oversight in healthcare; however it is not focused on conversational governance mechanisms or operational controls and provides no empirical evaluation of conversational systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python metadata title was corrupted; confirm full-text sections on governance and LLM deployment beyond provided excerpts before final inclusion tier.

appraisal.notes: Appraised as a journal perspective rather than empirical research; appropriate for opinion synthesis but limited transparency on literature selection and no primary data collection.

cerqual.explanation: Coherent argument linking AI opportunities to oversight and governance prerequisites in travel medicine, with clear statements on LLM limitations and clinical responsibility; adequacy is limited because the piece is non-systematic, non-empirical, and operational conversational governance detail is sparse in the provided text.

coding.theme: Responsible integration of AI and LLMs in regulated travel medicine
coding.subtheme: LLMs and chatbots as adjunctive travel health information tools under clinical oversight
rq_alignment: risk and compliance in regulated healthcare

synthesis.main_claim: AI, including generative models and LLMs such as ChatGPT, should be carefully validated and integrated as decision-support tools in travel medicine rather than replacing clinical expertise, with clinical oversight, explainability, accountability, and governance as prerequisites for responsible implementation.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a regulated healthcare perspective on balancing innovation and risk across the travel health continuum, explicitly positioning LLMs and chatbots as adjunctive information tools while stressing validation, regulatory oversight, monitoring, privacy, and equity considerations.
synthesis.limitations: Perspective format without described systematic methods or primary empirical sample; limited detail on operational conversational governance such as guardrails, logging, tracing, contestation, or audit mechanisms; LLM discussion is one section within a broader AI overview.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for human oversight, accountability, validation, and governance prerequisites when deploying LLMs and chatbots in regulated healthcare contexts; not suitable as central empirical evidence on conversational governance architectures or post-deployment operational controls.
